purpose: Firstcall PR2: people and the board. Salespeople, team leads, monitors and admins sign in; new leads wait in a team pool with live wait timers and urgency labels; the first salesperson to claim gets the lead; monitors place Unassigned leads, rescue Not-a-lead tray items and see who has waited longest; alerts go to the in-app inbox and web push, never to a buyer.
mechanism:
1. Accounts (firstcall/board/accounts.py, routes.py, core/access.py): argon2 passwords, cookie sessions that expire after session_days; setting a password ends the user's other sessions; roles salesperson, team lead, monitor, admin; leads.visible decides who sees a lead.
2. Claim (firstcall/board/leads.py): row locks so a lead is claimed once and is never owned by an inactive user or a non-member; a lost claim returns 409 'Already claimed by a teammate'; owned_since records when the current owner took the lead.
3. Clocks (core/hours.py, core/escalation.py, board/escalate.py): urgency labels and escalation count business minutes from the current pool stay (pool_since); time to claim counts from arrival; escalation fires once per stay; a rescue or placement starts a new stay; one team's bad hours config does not stop the others.
4. Tray and Unassigned (board/tray.py): rescue logs lead.rescued with who did it.
5. Alerts (board/alerts.py, outbound/dispatch.py, mail.py, push.py, allowlist.py): in-app inbox digests and web push; the allowlist never emails a buyer and refuses encoded-word or odd addresses; digests retry with backoff and are marked failed after email_retries; every alert is re-checked at send time against the recipient's current access; leaving a team cancels only alerts for leads the user can no longer see; push endpoints must be https on 443 to a host on push_hosts, both URL parsers must agree on the host, the rebuilt URL is sent, and each send is bounded to 5 s and 16 KB.
6. Pages (web/src, web/public/sw.js): Vite+TS pages built with textContent only; the service worker opens only same-origin paths; inbox links come only from server-built /leads/<id> paths; sign-out shows the sign-in page only after the server confirms.
7. Settings (firstcall/settings.py): base_url (beta refuses localhost), push_hosts (FIRSTCALL_PUSH_HOSTS), push_allow_http for local use only, email_retries, digest_seconds, session_days.
8. Migrations 0005-0008: users, sessions, memberships, pools, escalations per stay, digest retries, owned_since and inbox links.
decisions: Escalation and urgency count the current pool stay, not arrival, so a placed or rescued lead is not instantly late; time to claim still counts from arrival. Buyers come only from lead identities and contacts, never from tray messages, so one spam message cannot lock a user out. Push goes only to known push services (an allowlist, editable as a setting) rather than any https host, to close server-side request forgery. Rejected: letting a role-based alert be cancelled when someone leaves a team.
readers: README: people trying Firstcall or judging it. docs/adr: people judging design choices. docs/definitions.md: people reading the metrics. Code comments: the next maintainer.
